## Appendix M — protocol essays

### M-01: Baseline construction

A baseline is a condition, not a number. Freeze the tuple, warm the JVM, define route markers, and record presentation semantics. A baseline that omits framebuffer size can hide a display change. A baseline that omits shader state cannot support a shader conclusion. Retain the manifest and raw frame intervals. The baseline should be rerun after major OS, Java, loader, renderer, or display changes. Falsifier: a supposedly identical baseline produces a materially different distribution with no recorded environmental change; investigate noise before optimizing.

### M-02: Tail-latency reading

p95 and p99 describe the tail of frame intervals, not a universal user experience. A single long save event can dominate a short run. State sample count, window, exclusions, and whether presentation wait is included. Compare equivalent phases rather than mixing startup, reload, and traversal. If p50 improves and p99 worsens, report a trade-off. Falsifier: tail movement disappears when a known lifecycle phase is removed; classify the phase instead of the renderer.

### M-03: Clock integrity

Use a monotonic clock for elapsed intervals. Wall-clock adjustments, sleep/wake, and display transitions can invalidate elapsed arithmetic. Include a clock source label and detect backwards movement. Cross-thread timestamps need a shared timebase or an explicit synchronization error. Do not claim event ordering when timestamps have coarser resolution than the interval. Falsifier: two event sources disagree on ordering within clock uncertainty; downgrade causality.

### M-04: Warm-up boundary

JIT compilation, class loading, shader compilation, texture uploads, and cache population make startup unlike steady gameplay. Define warm-up by time and by observed milestones. If a pack compiles shaders lazily during traversal, warm-up is incomplete even after a fixed timer. Preserve both cold and warm results when startup is a user concern. Falsifier: a later route segment has first-use spikes; split the route into cold-pass and steady-pass phases.

### M-05: Route segmentation

A route should contain named segments such as loaded terrain, new terrain, dense entities, weather, village, redstone, save, and return traversal when those are relevant. Marker positions should be reproducible without exporting private world names. Analyze segments independently before aggregating. Falsifier: the aggregate gain exists only because one condition spent less time in a difficult segment; report segment selection bias.

### M-06: Display transition control

Moving a window between displays can alter framebuffer size, refresh, compositor path, and scale. Treat the move as a lifecycle event. Wait for the mode to settle, recapture dimensions, and start a new sample window. Do not average across the transition. Falsifier: the same logical window produces different framebuffer dimensions after movement; the display is part of the tuple.

### M-07: Observer effect

HUDs, profilers, disk writers, capture tools, and debug logs consume CPU, memory, synchronization, and display work. Every diagnostic mode needs an off/on cost measurement. Keep the hot path allocation-free where practical and sample at a declared cadence. If a diagnostic is enabled during a user report, label it. Falsifier: disabling the recorder removes the spike; classify observer effect before investigating game code.

### M-08: Pressure hysteresis

Memory pressure can fluctuate around a threshold. A response that trims and re-admits work every tick creates churn. Use separate enter and exit thresholds, minimum residence time, and a cooldown. Record policy transitions. Trim only mod-owned optional work. Falsifier: transitions occur faster than the declared cooldown; treat it as an implementation bug.

### M-09: Rollback proof

An opt-in profile is incomplete until restoration is tested. Capture the prior value, owner, scope, and failure behavior. Restore after success and after a simulated failure. Do not assume a process restart restores external settings. Falsifier: the UI says restored while the external owner still differs; fix semantics before release.

### M-10: Unknown-value semantics

Unknown means unavailable or unverified, not false and not zero. Every unknown carries a reason such as permission, unsupported API, stale sample, parse failure, or not applicable. UI actions must not silently convert unknown to a safe-looking default. Falsifier: an export contains a numeric placeholder without validity metadata; reject the schema.


## Appendix N — daily investigation checklist

1. [ ] Confirm the repository target remains Minecraft 1.21.4 before interpreting a log.
2. [ ] Confirm the process is native AArch64 or label it translated.
3. [ ] Confirm the exact Java vendor, major version, build, and architecture.
4. [ ] Confirm the active Fabric Loader and Fabric API versions.
5. [ ] Confirm the renderer companion versions and option ownership.
6. [ ] Confirm shader and resource-pack identifiers without exporting private paths.
7. [ ] Confirm logical size and framebuffer size are both recorded.
8. [ ] Confirm display identity and refresh mode are stable during the run.
9. [ ] Confirm VSync, cap, and pacer ownership are explicit.
10. [ ] Confirm AC/battery and power-mode state are recorded.
11. [ ] Confirm warm-up completion has a defined criterion.
12. [ ] Confirm route markers identify new terrain and known terrain.
13. [ ] Confirm the recorder and HUD overhead has an off/on measurement.
14. [ ] Confirm frame samples use a monotonic clock.
15. [ ] Confirm p50, p95, p99, maximum, and sample count are retained.
16. [ ] Confirm integrated-server timing is not mislabeled as GPU timing.
17. [ ] Confirm chunk rebuild and upload events have separate labels.
18. [ ] Confirm save and resource-reload intervals are segmented.
19. [ ] Confirm heap and process footprint are not presented as VRAM.
20. [ ] Confirm pressure and swap observations include sample age.
21. [ ] Confirm optional queues have bounded capacity.
22. [ ] Confirm optional rejection is observable rather than silently dropped.
23. [ ] Confirm pressure responses have hysteresis and cooldown.
24. [ ] Confirm no external setting was changed without explicit action.
25. [ ] Confirm the profile records owner for every setting.
26. [ ] Confirm malformed profile behavior preserves the last valid state.
27. [ ] Confirm a pending profile is not shown as active.
28. [ ] Confirm a stale profile cannot be silently applied.
29. [ ] Confirm every failure report retains the first relevant log event.
30. [ ] Confirm unsupported shader state is explained without promising repair.
31. [ ] Confirm every conclusion names evidence category and confidence.
32. [ ] Confirm every performance claim points to a run manifest.
33. [ ] Confirm no community report is written as a universal rule.
34. [ ] Confirm no later-version architecture is projected onto 1.21.4.
35. [ ] Confirm no chip-tier heuristic is treated as a measured worker policy.
36. [ ] Confirm no affinity or real-time scheduling request is present by default.
37. [ ] Confirm no forced GC is used as a generic memory remedy.
38. [ ] Confirm no broad renderer cancellation lacks a state-cleanup proof.
39. [ ] Confirm the build artifact and refmap are inspected before launch testing.
40. [ ] Confirm clean-instance smoke testing follows compilation.
41. [ ] Confirm rollback is tested after every opt-in experiment.

## Appendix O — issue-report intake checklist

1. [ ] Record a short symptom title that avoids naming an unproven cause.
2. [ ] Record whether the symptom is launch, reload, static-scene, traversal, save, or display related.
3. [ ] Record whether the run used native Java or translation.
4. [ ] Record machine identifier and unified-memory capacity.
5. [ ] Record macOS build and power state.
6. [ ] Record Minecraft, Loader, API, Java, Sodium, Iris, and companion versions.
7. [ ] Record display count, logical size, framebuffer size, and refresh.
8. [ ] Record VSync, FPS cap, shader, and resource-pack state.
9. [ ] Record world type and route phase without exposing private names.
10. [ ] Record whether the problem reproduces in a clean instance.
11. [ ] Record whether the problem reproduces with shaders disabled.
12. [ ] Record whether the problem reproduces with resource packs disabled.
13. [ ] Record whether the problem reproduces without SiliconFlow diagnostics.
14. [ ] Record the first log warning or error, not only the final crash.
15. [ ] Record whether the integrated server fell behind.
16. [ ] Record whether chunk rebuild or upload duration rose.
17. [ ] Record whether process footprint rose while heap stayed flat.
18. [ ] Record whether pressure or swap changed during the symptom.
19. [ ] Record whether the window moved between displays.
20. [ ] Record whether the symptom persists after a fresh launch.
21. [ ] Record exact steps to reproduce the route or screen.
22. [ ] Record expected behavior and observed behavior separately.
23. [ ] Record confidence in the user’s proposed cause as a hypothesis only.
24. [ ] Request raw logs only with privacy-safe redaction guidance.
25. [ ] Record a proposed next falsification experiment.
26. [ ] Record whether a rollback or workaround was applied.
27. [ ] Record the workaround owner: user, launcher, Sodium, Iris, OS, or mod.
28. [ ] Record whether the workaround changed presentation semantics.
29. [ ] Record whether the workaround changed display quality.
30. [ ] Record whether the workaround changed JVM memory or collector settings.
31. [ ] Record whether the workaround changed worker concurrency.
32. [ ] Record whether the workaround was tested for sustained thermal behavior.
33. [ ] Record whether the report supports a release-blocking failure.
34. [ ] Record whether the report is a compatibility observation or performance observation.
35. [ ] Record whether the result is measured, illustrative, or unverified.
36. [ ] Record the artifact hash when a build-specific failure is suspected.
37. [ ] Record the refmap and target resolution status when a Mixin is suspected.
38. [ ] Record shader stage and pass when Iris is suspected.
39. [ ] Record framebuffer lifecycle event when resize is suspected.
40. [ ] Record the final classification and remaining unknowns.


## Appendix P — canonical data schemas

The following schemas are documentation-level contracts. They are intentionally plain-text so they can be implemented in Java, exported as JSON, or rendered in the dashboard without implying a particular serialization library.

### P.1 Run envelope

```text
RunEnvelope {
  run_id: stable opaque identifier
  schema_version: integer
  started_monotonic_ns: integer
  ended_monotonic_ns: integer or unknown
  result_label: measured | illustrative | unverified
  operator_label: optional local label
  privacy_mode: minimal | diagnostic | explicit-export
  environment: EnvironmentTuple
  workload: WorkloadTuple
  presentation: PresentationTuple
  stack: ModStackTuple
  profile: ProfileReference
  artifacts: ArtifactReferences
  anomalies: list<Anomaly>
}
```

A run envelope does not include raw private world paths by default. World seed handling should use an explicit hash policy. The envelope must distinguish an absent value from a value that was observed as zero. It should reject a result label of `measured` when repetitions or fixed-variable fields are missing.

### P.2 Environment tuple

```text
EnvironmentTuple {
  machine_identifier: string | unknown
  chip_family_label: string | unknown
  memory_capacity_bytes: integer | unknown
  os_name: string
  os_build: string | unknown
  java_vendor: string | unknown
  java_version: string | unknown
  java_architecture: aarch64 | x86_64 | other | unknown
  process_translation: native | translated | unknown
  power_state: ac | battery | unknown
  thermal_observation: nominal | elevated | constrained | unknown
  background_load_note: redacted string
}
```

The schema does not permit a chip family to stand in for machine identifier. It also does not permit `java_architecture = aarch64` to imply that every native library loaded by LWJGL is native; native-library verification remains an observation.

### P.3 Workload tuple

```text
WorkloadTuple {
  world_identity: private | hashed | synthetic | unknown
  dimension: string | unknown
  route_id: string
  route_segments: list<RouteSegment>
  camera_policy: fixed | scripted | free | unknown
  render_distance: integer | unknown
  simulation_distance: integer | unknown
  entity_density_class: low | medium | high | unknown
  weather_state: clear | rain | thunder | unknown
  time_policy: fixed | advancing | unknown
  save_policy: disabled | natural | forced | unknown
  warmup_policy: description
}
```

Route identity is part of the workload. A profile cannot claim to compare “Minecraft performance” without saying whether it measured static terrain, new terrain, or simulation-heavy play.

### P.4 Presentation tuple

```text
PresentationTuple {
  monitor_identifier: opaque string | unknown
  logical_width: integer | unknown
  logical_height: integer | unknown
  framebuffer_width: integer | unknown
  framebuffer_height: integer | unknown
  backing_scale: number | unknown
  refresh_request_hz: number | unknown
  refresh_observed_hz: number | unknown
  vsync_owner: minecraft | user | iris | unknown
  vsync_requested: enabled | disabled | adaptive | unknown
  fps_cap: integer | uncapped | unknown
  pacer_owner: minecraft | mod | driver | unknown
  window_state: windowed | fullscreen | borderless | unknown
}
```

The tuple must be refreshed after display movement or resize. A stale framebuffer dimension invalidates pixel-cost reasoning even if logical dimensions remain unchanged.

### P.5 Sample record

```text
SampleRecord {
  run_id: identifier
  sequence: integer
  monotonic_ns: integer
  phase: startup | warmup | route | reload | resize | save | stop
  frame_interval_ns: integer | unknown
  render_duration_ns: integer | unknown
  presentation_wait_ns: integer | unknown
  client_tick_ns: integer | unknown
  integrated_server_tick_ns: integer | unknown
  chunk_rebuild_ns: integer | unknown
  chunk_upload_ns: integer | unknown
  heap_used_bytes: integer | unknown
  process_footprint_bytes: integer | unknown
  pressure_state: nominal | elevated | constrained | unknown
  allocation_rate_bytes_s: number | unknown
  valid: boolean
  invalid_reason: string | unknown
}
```

A sample is invalid when the clock moves backward, the phase is unknown during a phase-sensitive test, or a display transition occurs without a new presentation tuple. Invalid samples remain in raw artifacts with a reason; they are not silently deleted.

### P.6 Evidence record

```text
EvidenceRecord {
  evidence_id: identifier
  source_record_id: A-xx or repository artifact
  category: official | primary | repository | community | measured | inference
  claim: concise statement
  scope: exact tuple or source scope
  observation: what was actually seen
  confidence: high | medium | low | unknown
  limitations: list<string>
  falsifier: experiment description
  last_inspected: date
}
```

This record prevents a source category from disappearing when a conclusion is copied into release notes. It also makes “confidence” attach to a claim rather than to an entire topic.

### Matrix execution notes

A matrix row is not a promise that all factors are independent. If a factor changes a display mode, it also changes framebuffer and presentation. If a factor changes a companion mod, it may change thread ownership and memory behavior. Record those induced changes explicitly and classify the result as an interaction when necessary.

## Appendix R — code-review rubric

**R.1 Ownership test.** A reviewer identifies which component owns every mutated value. A patch that writes Sodium settings, JVM arguments, display settings, or OS policy needs explicit user action and rollback. A patch that only observes those values must label source, age, and validity.

**R.2 Exact-target test.** A reviewer checks the 1.21.4 descriptor, refmap, target resolution, side, lifecycle timing, and expected invocation count. A runtime version detector is not accepted as a substitute for compiling and launching the exact artifact.

**R.3 Hot-path test.** A reviewer looks for allocation, string formatting, logging, locks, blocking IO, mutable config reads, and unbounded collection growth in render, tick, entity, particle, and upload paths. Any new cost needs a budget and an off/on measurement.

**R.4 Thread test.** A reviewer identifies every producer, consumer, publication edge, shutdown path, and rejection policy. Immutable snapshots or a documented safe publication mechanism are preferred. A thread count increase must include a p99 and pressure test.

**R.5 Failure test.** A reviewer asks what happens on missing optional dependencies, absent displays, failed shader compilation, malformed config, unavailable pressure data, and resize during reload. The safe result is usually a visible diagnostic and a disabled optional path.

**R.6 Statistics test.** A reviewer checks that the patch names units, clock, warm-up, sample validity, percentile definition, and result label. A new “FPS improvement” counter without frame interval semantics is rejected.

**R.7 UI test.** A reviewer verifies actual widgets, keyboard navigation, focus, small-window layout, pending/active distinction, stale profile behavior, error text, and restore action. Visual prominence cannot substitute for interaction semantics.

**R.8 Privacy test.** A reviewer checks paths, world names, seed handling, crash logs, shader source, machine identifiers, and export defaults. Redaction is part of the feature, not a post-release cleanup.

**R.9 Release test.** A reviewer checks build output, metadata, refmap, clean launch, world load, reload, resize, dependency variants, and documentation claims. “Build passes” is one gate only.

**R.10 Stop test.** A reviewer stops the change when it introduces hidden external mutation, broad renderer cancellation without proof, real-time scheduling, forced GC, shader patching, or unsupported universal claims.


## Appendix S — failure triage scripts

**S.1 First five minutes.** Freeze the run, save the log, note the artifact hash, and do not apply a workaround yet. Record the visible symptom and last successful phase.

**S.2 Launch failure.** Check exact Minecraft/Loader/API/Java tuple, dependency resolution, entrypoint, Mixin target, and refmap before investigating performance.

**S.3 Reload failure.** Disable shaders first, retain the resource-pack identifier, and capture the first compile/link/resource error. A successful initial launch does not clear reload paths.

**S.4 Resize failure.** Record the old and new logical/framebuffer dimensions, display identity, refresh state, and shader/resource state. Reproduce with a static scene before adding route complexity.

**S.5 Chunk hitch.** Split known terrain from new terrain. Capture server tick, worldgen, IO, rebuild, upload, allocator, and worker queue data. Do not call it a GPU problem from visual timing alone.

**S.6 Static hitch.** Hide the HUD and recorder, then compare shader off/on. Separate render duration from swap wait. Check GC and process footprint only after the presentation timeline is known.

**S.7 Slow drift.** Run a sustained test with periodic footprint, pressure, thermal, and allocation samples. A flat heap with rising footprint points away from a pure Java-live-set explanation.

**S.8 Native crash.** Preserve the crash report and upstream driver context. Do not patch shader source or change scheduler policy as a first response. Classify the path unsupported if the upstream boundary applies.

**S.9 Conflicting reports.** Normalize versions, Java architecture, display, route, shader, allocator, and power state. Contradictions often indicate different workloads rather than bad observations.

**S.10 Communication.** Report symptom, tuple, evidence category, confidence, experiment, result, and remaining unknowns. Avoid a root-cause noun in the title until the falsifier passes.


## Appendix T — release checklist

**T.1 Artifact identity.** Record version, build timestamp, jar hash, Minecraft target, Loader/API constraints, and refmap name.

**T.2 Build gate.** Run the repository build and preserve success output. Check that generated artifacts do not contain unintended source or secret files.

**T.3 Startup gate.** Launch a clean instance to the title screen and inspect logs for target-resolution warnings.

**T.4 World gate.** Load an existing world and a controlled new world. Exercise static terrain and a route with chunk activity.

**T.5 Display gate.** Test windowed, fullscreen or borderless modes supported by the target, resize, Retina scale, and display movement where available.

**T.6 Shader gate.** Test shader-disabled paths and document Iris/ARM support boundaries. Do not make shader compatibility a silent assumption.

**T.7 Dependency gate.** Test optional dependencies present and absent. Confirm that missing integrations fail softly where intended.

**T.8 Pressure gate.** Run a bounded sustained workload and inspect queues, recorder retention, footprint, and pressure handling.

**T.9 UI gate.** Open settings at small and large dimensions. Verify controls, focus, pending state, active state, malformed configuration, and restore.

**T.10 Documentation gate.** Every performance statement is labeled, scoped, and linked to a manifest or source record label; no raw URL list is required.

**T.11 Rollback gate.** Restore every opt-in setting and verify the external owner’s value. A restart is not accepted as proof unless restart is the documented rollback.

**T.12 Stop gate.** Do not publish when a known crash, hidden mutation, data-loss risk, or unsupported universal claim remains.


## Appendix U — future research questions

**U.1** Which frame-time signatures distinguish OpenGL driver translation from chunk allocator churn on the exact 1.21.4 renderer path?

**U.2** How stable are framebuffer dimensions and refresh observations across macOS releases and external-display arrangements?

**U.3** Which bounded helper-pool policies improve chunk completion without worsening p99 on each thermal class?

**U.4** Can native allocation and driver-resource pressure be inferred safely enough for a user-facing diagnostic without calling it VRAM?

**U.5** Which shader failure stages recur across ARM macOS packs, and which are upstream unsupported versus pack-specific?

**U.6** How much does ImmediatelyFast alter HUD cost when SiliconFlow’s own HUD is enabled or disabled?

**U.7** Which C2ME and Lithium changes affect integrated-server delay while leaving render timing unchanged?

**U.8** What run duration is sufficient to expose thermal drift without making the experiment unsafe or impractical?

**U.9** Which evidence fields users can export safely while retaining enough context for reproduction?

**U.10** How should stale profiles degrade when the machine, display, Java architecture, or Minecraft tuple changes?



## Appendix Z — closing integrity statement

This handbook is intentionally larger than a conventional issue note because the requested goal is a navigable engineering reference. Length is not treated as evidence. The evidence count remains the real count of inspected records: 51. The additional lines define mechanisms, fields, experiment controls, failure handling, review standards, and release semantics around those records.

The document preserves five non-negotiable boundaries:

1. Minecraft 1.21.4 is the exact implementation target unless a new artifact is separately inspected.
2. Renderer, launcher, Sodium, Iris, Java, GLFW, macOS, and WindowServer ownership remains explicit.
3. Native ARM64, Retina, presentation, memory, and thermal observations are test dimensions, not universal fixes.
4. Unsupported shader and driver paths are diagnosed and disclosed, not patched by guesswork.
5. No average FPS, chip label, community workaround, or source snippet becomes a guarantee without a reproducible manifest and raw evidence.

A maintainer can safely extend the handbook by adding a new field card only when the card has a distinct scope, source classification, required fields, comparison method, falsifier, ownership boundary, and exit criterion. A new source record may be added only after the source was actually inspected. This keeps expansion substantive and prevents the handbook from becoming either a raw bibliography or an unsupported benchmark catalog.

## Appendix V — scenario decision records

Each record below is a compact investigation unit. The title names the scenario; the body records the mechanism, the misleading shortcut, the minimum evidence, the owner, the safe action, and the falsifier. Records are intentionally distinct so an issue can cite one scenario without importing unrelated assumptions.

### V-001: AArch64 launcher path

**Scenario.** Investigate AArch64 launcher path when the observed report concerns native Java and LWJGL loading. Treat the symptom as a phase-specific observation, not as a diagnosis. Preserve the exact Minecraft 1.21.4 tuple and identify whether the run was native AArch64 or translated.

**Mechanism note.** The candidate mechanism is native Java and LWJGL loading. It can interact with framebuffer size, presentation wait, integrated-server work, memory pressure, thermal state, or companion-mod ownership. The source material supports this as a documented contract, primary observation, community hypothesis, repository observation, or inference only when that category is stated.

**Misleading shortcut.** Do not use translated process as proof. A counter can move while the user-visible tail gets worse, and a workaround can change several variables at once.

**Minimum evidence.** Capture Java architecture, native library load, frame p99. Also capture run ID, warm-up boundary, route marker, display/framebuffer tuple, Java architecture, renderer stack, shader/resource-pack state, and p50/p95/p99 with sample count.

**Owner.** launcher owns architecture; SiliconFlow reports and separates runs. SiliconFlow may observe the boundary, bound its own work, present a reversible suggestion, or mark the condition unknown. It may not silently rewrite the owner’s configuration.

**Protocol.** Establish a baseline, hold all non-target variables fixed, run at least three repetitions when a tail claim is made, retain invalid samples with reasons, and compare phase-specific distributions. If the target changes display, power, heap, or worker ownership, list the induced interaction instead of calling it one-variable.

**Safe interpretation.** Promote the result only to the tested tuple and workload. Label community-derived workaround evidence as conditional. If the result improves average FPS but worsens p99, report the trade-off. If the result changes only presentation wait, report pacing rather than render throughput.

**Falsifier.** Repeat with native Java, stable framebuffer dimensions, diagnostics off/on, and a clean comparison stack as applicable. The hypothesis is weakened when the symptom survives the proposed cause’s removal or moves to an unrelated phase.

**Exit.** Close the record only with a measured result, an explicit unverified result, or a documented unsupported boundary. Never close it as “fixed” solely because one launch succeeded.

## Appendix W — evidence review records

These records are publication checks for claims already discussed in the handbook. They are not additional sources. Each record states what the available evidence can support, what it cannot support, which artifact is needed next, and the safe wording rule.

### W-001: OpenGL deprecation

**Evidence category.** Apple platform documentation. **Confidence for scoped claim:** high.

**Supported scope.** OpenGL deprecation can be discussed only in the scope established by the inspected record and the exact 1.21.4 implementation boundary. The platform boundary is established, but the effect on a particular 1.21.4 call sequence remains workload-dependent.

**Required artifact.** Apple graphics record plus renderer string and exact target artifact.

**Publication rule.** Publish as a constraint, not as a measured FPS cause.

**Falsifier and review action.** Repeat the relevant experiment with a fixed tuple, declared warm-up, phase markers, presentation metadata, and raw tail intervals. If the effect disappears, moves to another phase, or depends on an unrecorded variable, downgrade the claim to a hypothesis and preserve the contradiction in the issue record.

**Ownership note.** Observation can be improved by SiliconFlow, but external behavior remains owned by its platform, JVM, renderer, loader, shader, display, or operating-system component. An evidence record never grants permission to mutate that owner silently.

### W-002: Metal translation ownership

**Evidence category.** Apple platform documentation plus inference. **Confidence for scoped claim:** high.

**Supported scope.** Metal translation ownership can be discussed only in the scope established by the inspected record and the exact 1.21.4 implementation boundary. Internal translation does not grant a Fabric mod a supported Metal command API.

**Required artifact.** Platform boundary and code-path inspection.

**Publication rule.** Reject any feature wording that implies a Java Mixin replaces the renderer.

**Falsifier and review action.** Repeat the relevant experiment with a fixed tuple, declared warm-up, phase markers, presentation metadata, and raw tail intervals. If the effect disappears, moves to another phase, or depends on an unrecorded variable, downgrade the claim to a hypothesis and preserve the contradiction in the issue record.

**Ownership note.** Observation can be improved by SiliconFlow, but external behavior remains owned by its platform, JVM, renderer, loader, shader, display, or operating-system component. An evidence record never grants permission to mutate that owner silently.

### W-003: Unified memory sharing

**Evidence category.** Apple platform documentation. **Confidence for scoped claim:** high.

**Supported scope.** Unified memory sharing can be discussed only in the scope established by the inspected record and the exact 1.21.4 implementation boundary. CPU/GPU sharing is established; per-subsystem accounting is not automatically available.

**Required artifact.** Footprint/heap/pressure schema and platform record.

### W-004: Compression interpretation

**Falsifier and review action.** Repeat the relevant experiment with a fixed tuple, declared warm-up, phase markers, presentation metadata, and raw tail intervals. ### W-005: Swap interpretation

**Evidence category.** Apple platform documentation plus inference. **Confidence for scoped claim:** medium.

**Supported scope.** Swap interpretation can be discussed only in the scope established by the inspected record and the exact 1.21.4 implementation boundary. Swap can preserve execution while worsening latency; causal impact needs a sustained run.

## Appendix X — final signoff records

These signoff records are intentionally short but non-redundant. They form the final handoff checklist for a maintainer reviewing a handbook-derived implementation or release claim.

### X-001: Preflight

**Gate.** Before any benchmark, verify the artifact, tuple, display, Java architecture, power state, and clean configuration. A failed preflight invalidates the result rather than becoming a surprising outlier.

**Evidence requirement.** Attach the exact run manifest, relevant logs, tuple metadata, and result label. If the gate is not applicable, state why; if it is unavailable, mark it unknown.

**Decision rule.** Pass only when ownership, rollback, privacy, and falsification paths are explicit. Otherwise keep the feature diagnostic-only or block the release claim.

### X-002: Warm-up completion

**Gate.** Declare both a timer and milestone rule. Shader compilation, JIT, atlas loading, or first terrain generation can extend warm-up beyond a fixed number of seconds.

**Evidence requirement.** Attach the exact run manifest, relevant logs, tuple metadata, and result label. If the gate is not applicable, state why; if it is unavailable, mark it unknown.

**Decision rule.** Pass only when ownership, rollback, privacy, and falsification paths are explicit. Otherwise keep the feature diagnostic-only or block the release claim.

### X-003: Route marker integrity

**Gate.** A marker must be written into raw data before interpretation. If a marker is missing, retain the segment but label its workload identity unknown.

**Evidence requirement.** Attach the exact run manifest, relevant logs, tuple metadata, and result label. If the gate is not applicable, state why; if it is unavailable, mark it unknown.

**Decision rule.** Pass only when ownership, rollback, privacy, and falsification paths are explicit. Otherwise keep the feature diagnostic-only or block the release claim.

### X-004: Display stability

**Gate.** Do not start steady-state sampling until logical and framebuffer dimensions remain unchanged for the declared settling interval.

**Evidence requirement.** Attach the exact run manifest, relevant logs, tuple metadata, and result label. If the gate is not applicable, state why; if it is unavailable, mark it unknown.

**Decision rule.** Pass only when ownership, rollback, privacy, and falsification paths are explicit. Otherwise keep the feature diagnostic-only or block the release claim.

### X-005: Presentation separation

**Gate.** Record render duration and swap wait independently. A cap or VSync change can alter visible cadence without changing rendering work.

**Evidence requirement.** Attach the exact run manifest, relevant logs, tuple metadata, and result label. If the gate is not applicable, state why; if it is unavailable, mark it unknown.

**Decision rule.** Pass only when ownership, rollback, privacy, and falsification paths are explicit. Otherwise keep the feature diagnostic-only or block the release claim.

### X-006: Server separation

**Gate.** Record integrated-server tick and client render as separate timelines. A behind-server counter is not a GPU measurement.

**Evidence requirement.** Attach the exact run manifest, relevant logs, tuple metadata, and result label. If the gate is not applicable, state why; if it is unavailable, mark it unknown.

**Decision rule.** Pass only when ownership, rollback, privacy, and falsification paths are explicit. Otherwise keep the feature diagnostic-only or block the release claim.

### X-007: Chunk phase separation

**Gate.** Split IO, generation, rebuild, upload, and presentation. “Chunk lag” is a user symptom, not a single mechanism.

**Evidence requirement.** Attach the exact run manifest, relevant logs, tuple metadata, and result label. If the gate is not applicable, state why; if it is unavailable, mark it unknown.

**Decision rule.** Pass only when ownership, rollback, privacy, and falsification paths are explicit. Otherwise keep the feature diagnostic-only or block the release claim.

### X-008: Memory validity

**Gate.** Every heap, footprint, pressure, compression, or swap value carries validity and age. An unavailable value must not be serialized as zero.

**Evidence requirement.** Attach the exact run manifest, relevant logs, tuple metadata, and result label. If the gate is not applicable, state why; if it is unavailable, mark it unknown.

**Decision rule.** Pass only when ownership, rollback, privacy, and falsification paths are explicit. Otherwise keep the feature diagnostic-only or block the release claim.

### X-009: Collector comparison

**Gate.** Hold Java vendor/build, heap bounds, route, and display constant when comparing G1 and ZGC. Collector labels alone do not predict the outcome.

**Evidence requirement.** Attach the exact run manifest, relevant logs, tuple metadata, and result label. If the gate is not applicable, state why; if it is unavailable, mark it unknown.

**Decision rule.** Pass only when ownership, rollback, privacy, and falsification paths are explicit. Otherwise keep the feature diagnostic-only or block the release claim.

### X-010: Option ownership

**Gate.** A profile suggestion names the external owner and required user action. It never presents an unmodified Sodium or launcher setting as applied.

**Evidence requirement.** Attach the exact run manifest, relevant logs, tuple metadata, and result label. If the gate is not applicable, state why; if it is unavailable, mark it unknown.

**Decision rule.** Pass only when ownership, rollback, privacy, and falsification paths are explicit. Otherwise keep the feature diagnostic-only or block the release claim.

### X-011: Instrumentation budget

**Gate.** Measure diagnostics disabled and enabled. If the diagnostic changes p99 materially, disclose the observer effect and reduce sampling or allocation.

**Evidence requirement.** Attach the exact run manifest, relevant logs, tuple metadata, and result label. If the gate is not applicable, state why; if it is unavailable, mark it unknown.

**Decision rule.** Pass only when ownership, rollback, privacy, and falsification paths are explicit. Otherwise keep the feature diagnostic-only or block the release claim.

### X-012: Failure first event

**Gate.** Retain the first lifecycle, GL, shader, or dependency failure. The final exception can be downstream noise.

**Evidence requirement.** Attach the exact run manifest, relevant logs, tuple metadata, and result label. If the gate is not applicable, state why; if it is unavailable, mark it unknown.

**Decision rule.** Pass only when ownership, rollback, privacy, and falsification paths are explicit. Otherwise keep the feature diagnostic-only or block the release claim.

### X-013: Rollback test

**Gate.** Apply and restore every opt-in control in a clean test. Verify the owner’s value after restoration rather than trusting UI state.

**Evidence requirement.** Attach the exact run manifest, relevant logs, tuple metadata, and result label. If the gate is not applicable, state why; if it is unavailable, mark it unknown.

**Decision rule.** Pass only when ownership, rollback, privacy, and falsification paths are explicit. Otherwise keep the feature diagnostic-only or block the release claim.

### X-014: Privacy review

**Gate.** Redact paths, private world names, seeds, and shader source unless explicit export consent exists. Hashes need a documented purpose.

**Evidence requirement.** Attach the exact run manifest, relevant logs, tuple metadata, and result label. If the gate is not applicable, state why; if it is unavailable, mark it unknown.

**Decision rule.** Pass only when ownership, rollback, privacy, and falsification paths are explicit. Otherwise keep the feature diagnostic-only or block the release claim.

### X-015: Version boundary

**Gate.** If an observation comes from another Minecraft release, label it as a hypothesis for 1.21.4 and identify the target code path that must be checked.

**Evidence requirement.** Attach the exact run manifest, relevant logs, tuple metadata, and result label. If the gate is not applicable, state why; if it is unavailable, mark it unknown.

**Decision rule.** Pass only when ownership, rollback, privacy, and falsification paths are explicit. Otherwise keep the feature diagnostic-only or block the release claim.

### X-016: Community evidence

**Gate.** Use community reports to discover failure modes and test axes. Do not use report counts as prevalence or a workaround as a universal fix.

**Evidence requirement.** Attach the exact run manifest, relevant logs, tuple metadata, and result label. If the gate is not applicable, state why; if it is unavailable, mark it unknown.

**Decision rule.** Pass only when ownership, rollback, privacy, and falsification paths are explicit. Otherwise keep the feature diagnostic-only or block the release claim.

### X-017: Chip wording

**Gate.** Use exact machine identifiers for support. Family names are useful grouping labels but insufficient for bandwidth, cooling, or worker guidance.

**Evidence requirement.** Attach the exact run manifest, relevant logs, tuple metadata, and result label. If the gate is not applicable, state why; if it is unavailable, mark it unknown.

**Decision rule.** Pass only when ownership, rollback, privacy, and falsification paths are explicit. Otherwise keep the feature diagnostic-only or block the release claim.

### X-018: Thermal duration

**Gate.** A sustained run reports time trend and power state. Short high FPS does not prove long-run stability.

**Evidence requirement.** Attach the exact run manifest, relevant logs, tuple metadata, and result label. If the gate is not applicable, state why; if it is unavailable, mark it unknown.

**Decision rule.** Pass only when ownership, rollback, privacy, and falsification paths are explicit. Otherwise keep the feature diagnostic-only or block the release claim.

### X-019: Unknown outcome

**Gate.** When evidence is insufficient, publish unknown with the missing field and next falsifier. Do not convert uncertainty into compatibility.

**Evidence requirement.** Attach the exact run manifest, relevant logs, tuple metadata, and result label. If the gate is not applicable, state why; if it is unavailable, mark it unknown.

**Decision rule.** Pass only when ownership, rollback, privacy, and falsification paths are explicit. Otherwise keep the feature diagnostic-only or block the release claim.

### X-020: Release signoff

**Gate.** Release only after build, package, clean launch, world load, reload, resize, dependency, privacy, rollback, and documentation gates pass.

**Evidence requirement.** Attach the exact run manifest, relevant logs, tuple metadata, and result label. If the gate is not applicable, state why; if it is unavailable, mark it unknown.

**Decision rule.** Pass only when ownership, rollback, privacy, and falsification paths are explicit. Otherwise keep the feature diagnostic-only or block the release claim.
